body:
Founder: 'ok now lets fix rubber banding jumps'. Per S459-68's own named lesson (finite-difference velocity estimation is unsafe across a changing-acceleration interval like a jump), the real fix: NetPlayer gained real vx/vy/vz fields (72->84 bytes), server_broadcast populates them from the server's exact PlayerState velocity, client reconciliation now sets p->vx/vy/vz directly from the server's real value instead of guessing. Live-verified: real vy values on the wire matched the true physics arc exactly during a live jump test. Found and fixed a real, independent, pre-existing bug along the way: apps2/emily-bot's Go decoder had netPlayerSize stuck at 68 bytes since before kill_streak grew the struct to 72 -- every multi-entity snapshot has been misdecoding every entity after the first since then. Fixed. go build/test (all packages) and python -m unittest (35 tests) green. Live server + bot pool redeployed together (protocol change requires matched builds), fresh Windows client built. Commit 38f114b.

⚓ ☃
title: S459-69: real fix for jump rubberbanding -- put velocity on the wire
